can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of verbs followed by an '-ing' form.
example_raw:
[talking about cars] ... we can't avoid using them because we are used to them. (Turkey; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Turkish; Pass)

I couldn't stand being there. (Japan; B2 VANTAGE; 1998; Japanese; Pass)

Moreover we may consider offering bonus schemes, to increase the staff's loyalty to our company. (Russia; B2 VANTAGE; 2010; Russian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Conceptualising actions as objects of verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a verb to describe the process of doing another verb.

positives: I couldn't stand being there.
We may consider offering bonus schemes.

can_do_statement: Can use some verbs connected with the senses + direct object + an '-ing' form, to give emphasis to an ongoing activity.
example_raw:
Then I heard someone screaming, I was afraid and I said to the others: "Let's go out, something is happening". (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Greek; Pass)

I think we can learn nothing by seeing animals out of their habitat: we cannot see them running or eating or hunting. (Italy; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Italian; Fail)

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing an ongoing activity through sensory perception.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Describing what you saw or heard happening.

positives: Then I heard someone screaming.
We cannot see them running.
negatives: I saw the man in the street.

guideword: FORM/USE: VERBS OF SENSES + OBJECT + INFINITIVE
can_do_statement: Can use some verbs connected with the senses + direct object + infinitive without 'to' emphasising a complete action.
example_raw:
I would like to see it develop without any pollution and without destroying the environment. (Greece; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2003; Greek; Fail)

Nowadays, it is very common in Argentina to hear people talk about the economic depression. (Argentina; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2002; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Emphasizing a complete action through sensory perception.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Describing a full event you witnessed.

positives: I would like to see it develop.
It is common to hear people talk about it.
negatives: I like to hear the music.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would hate' + 'to' infinitive, for emphasis.
example_raw:
We in the student committee would hate to see all that space go to waste. (Sweden; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2001; Swedish; Fail)

I am very much aware of my parents’ mistakes and would hate to make the same ones. (Switzerland; C2 MASTERY; 1993; French; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Expressing a strong negative preference about a hypothetical situation.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Saying you really wouldn't want something to happen.

positives: I would hate to see all that space go to waste.
I'd really hate to make the same mistakes.
negatives: I would like to see it.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of phrasal verbs + object pronoun + particle.
example_raw:
I heard about this club when I was watching T.V. and I wanted to check it out. (B1, French)

I really like shopping for clothes, but I hate trying them on because always when I finish, the shop assistant shows me more clothes. (B1, Portuguese)

So, think it over and tell me what you decide to do. (B1, Russian)

ontology.mental_model: Manipulating specific, previously mentioned entities with a phrasal verb.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a pronoun in the middle of a phrasal verb.

positives: I wanted to check it out.
I hate trying them on.
negatives: I wanted to check out the book.
I hate to try on the clothes.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs + particle + object.
example_raw:
Were it not for my university, I would give up this class immediately. (B1, Russian)

I must travel to Mexico City because I won a novel contest and I need to pick up my award. (B1, Spanish - Latin American)

So I opened the envelope and took out the letter. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

She turned off the phone and walked to the bathroom. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Manipulating entities with an inseparable or unseparated phrasal verb.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Keeping the verb and particle together before the object.

positives: I need to pick up my award.
She turned off the phone.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs without an object.
example_raw:
I'm going to get up early on Saturday. (A2, Portuguese)

Shall we go out this weekend to a concert? (Argentina; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

We can meet up at 2 pm. (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Portuguese; Pass)

If you have time, you can come over and I will introduce you to my friends. (Malaysia; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Chinese; Pass)

Every day I can see the sea when I wake up. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2000; Spanish - European; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Describing actions that are self-contained without affecting external entities.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a phrasal verb that doesn't need an object.

positives: I'm going to get up early.
We can meet up at 2 pm.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of phrasal verbs without an object.
example_raw:
Some species are dying out, and keeping such animals in zoos where they can give life to new generations is the only way to prevent them from becoming completely extinct. (B2 Polish)

The following day my grandpa didn’t show up. (B2 Greek)

If you are not good enough at reading, you'll end up wasting your time. (B2, Japanese)

ontology.mental_model: Describing complex, self-contained actions with advanced phrasal verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using advanced phrasal verbs without an object.

positives: Some species are dying out.
The following day my grandpa didn't show up.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of phrasal verbs + object pronoun + particle.
example_raw:
I will pick you up and arrange everything. (A2 Burmese)

Ring me up or send me an email if you have any questions. (A2 Basque)

You may need to throw it away, it'll be too dirty after painting. (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Thai; Pass)

Could you come here by nine o'clock to help me out? (Brazil; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Manipulating specific entities with common phrasal verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Putting a pronoun in the middle of a simple phrasal verb.

positives: I will pick you up tomorrow.
Ring me up if you have questions.
negatives: I will pick up the bag.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of phrasal verbs without an object.
example_raw:
I needed to hang out because my life was too jam-packed and hectic. (B1, Italian)

[talking about a phone] Its battery had run out. (B1, Portuguese)

She cried a lot. Her feelings, emotions were all scattered. But Lisa didn't give up. (B1, Vietnamese)

ontology.mental_model: Describing intermediate self-contained actions with phrasal verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using intermediate phrasal verbs without an object.

positives: I needed to hang out.
Its battery had run out.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of phrasal verbs + object pronoun + particle.
example_raw:
[talking about a band] I went to check them out last week and here is my review of the two concerts. (Denmark; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 1998; Danish; Pass)

[talking about a living room] I tried to clean it up as much as possible. (Sweden; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2003; Swedish; Pass)

[talking about setting up an office phone system] We just need a small set and a little time to fix it up. (China; C1 EFFECTIVE OPERATIONAL PROFICIENCY; 2002; Chinese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Manipulating specific entities with advanced phrasal verbs.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Putting a pronoun in the middle of an advanced phrasal verb.

positives: I went to check them out last week.
I tried to clean it up.

can_do_statement: Can use phrasal verbs + nouns as object + particle.
example_raw:
I am glad that you have decided to take some time off and more glad because you are going to the U.S. (Chile; B2 VANTAGE; 2001; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

Another way is also to turn the computers off in the evenings. (B2 VANTAGE; 2009; Swedish; Pass)

It was necessary to call the electrician up. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Spanish - European; Pass)

If we can make these improvements, we might be able to work this problem out. (France; B2 VANTAGE; 2010; French; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Separating a phrasal verb with a full noun phrase.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Putting a noun between the verb and the particle.

positives: Another way is also to turn the computers off.
It was necessary to call the electrician up.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of phrasal verbs + particle + object.
example_raw:
I don't need to use my imagination while I'm surfing the internet, but if I'm reading a book I can build up the whole surroundings and the characters in my own head. (B2, German)

I had already booked my seat on the ferry-boat to Athens and I couldn't put off my crossing. (B2, Italian)

I can surf the internet and look up some useful information. (B2, Chinese)

The concert finished very late and after the concert I had to clean up the hall. (B2, French)

ontology.mental_model: Keeping advanced phrasal verbs together before an object.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using an advanced phrasal verb with an object.

positives: I can build up the whole surroundings.
I couldn't put off my crossing.
negatives: I couldn't put my crossing off.

can_do_statement: Can use 'look forward to' as a fixed expression followed by an '-ing' form or noun phrase, usually at the end of correspondence.
example_raw:
I'm looking forward to seeing you! (Turkey; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Turkish; Pass)

I look forward to hearing from you. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Polish; Pass)

I am looking forward to our meeting. (Sri Lanka; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Singhalese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Anticipating a future event with pleasure.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using 'look forward to' before an -ing verb or noun.

positives: I am looking forward to seeing you!
I look forward to our meeting.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of verb + particle + preposition + noun or pronoun.
example_raw:
I can look up to someone in admiration if he (or she) is dedicating his (or her) life to helping other people. (Switzerland; B2 VANTAGE; 2005; Swiss German; Pass)

Other people will see you as a knowledgeable person and they will look up to you. (Greece; B2 VANTAGE; 2008; Greek; Pass)

You should face up to the problem and tell everybody the truth, that you are working too hard. (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Polish; Pass)

We couldn't just swim and eat ice-cream every day of our summer vacation, so we sat down and came up with the craziest idea ever. (Sweden; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Swedish; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: Directing an action towards an entity using a three-part phrasal verb.
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Using a phrasal verb with three parts.

positives: I can look up to someone in admiration.
We sat down and came up with the craziest idea.
negatives: I looked up at the sky.
